conviction_note: Near-non-result: the company-level facts (Q2 release, call guidance, a Sept 11 8-K on the Chief Banking Officer leaving, insider sales) are all public. The peer prints since BFST last spoke split: Baton Rouge peer Investar beat on NIM, Lafayette peer Home Bancorp missed on credit, and Gulf/Texas peers showed deposit costs rising after the 16 Sept Fed hike. The findings sum to -0.25 and the scaled number is (2x0.49-1)x4.0 = -0.08. Both are small and agree in sign. p_up sits at 49 because the negatives are proxies and the stock sits 1% under its 52-week high with five Buy ratings.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $0.74 from two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/BFST) and Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BFST/earnings-forecasts, which also gives revenue $93.3M). A third page shows $0.75. Q2 2026 printed $0.70 GAAP and $0.71 core (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001624322/000162432226000032/exhibit991_earningsrelease.htm). The company gives no numeric guidance in its release. On the call (Quartr summary, https://quartr.com/events/business-first-bancshares-inc-bfst-q2-2026_oCaybdfZ) management guided to high single-digit annualized loan growth in Q3 and Q4, falling core expenses, no further rate cuts assumed, and a 1.25% ROA exiting Q4 (Q2 core ROAA was 1.05%). A secondary summary puts core opex at about $58M in Q3 and $57M in Q4, against Q2's $58.4M.
positioning_check: Short interest 1,236,013 shares, 4.03% of float, 5.7 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30. That is up 11.2% from 1,111,825 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BFST/short-interest/, FINRA publication 2026-10-09). It is a moderate short that is building, not a crowded one, though 5.7 days to cover is meaningful on a thin name (20d average volume about 184k shares). The option chain is unusable: no two-sided ATM quotes, so there is no skew and no implied move. The baseline anchor is the median historical reaction, 3.85%. Tape: spot $31.91, 1.15% below the 52-week high, +3.4% over 20 days, 20-day realised vol 15%. Five analysts, all Buy, targets $34.50-$36 after late-July raises.

findings.finding: Investar, the closest Baton Rouge peer (BFST is also headquartered in Baton Rouge), reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-22, after BFST last spoke. NIM rose 6 bps to 3.73%; GAAP EPS was $0.74 and core EPS $0.77 against a ~$0.75 consensus. This points to margin still widening for south Louisiana commercial banks through Q3, which is the line BFST's $0.71 to $0.74 consensus step depends on (Q2 NIM was 3.73%, +8 bps).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 (2026-07-23, amc) BFST printed NIM +8 bps with core EPS $0.71 roughly in line, and the stock moved +2.26%. Its +6.88% (2025-10-23) and +8.84% (2025-01-23) reactions both followed margin-led quarters, per the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print from three sessions ago on a different name. BFST's consensus ($0.74) has not visibly moved since and its 5-day run-up is only +1.9%. If the read-through were priced, BFST estimates or the price would have stepped up after 10-22.
findings.independence: Hancock Whitney's Q3 NIM was also +5 bps (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000750577/000119312526426654/hwc-ex99_1.htm), but 4 bps of that came from acquisition accretion. Different document, partly the same direction. Proxy only: BFST's own Q3 margin is unknown.

findings.finding: Home Bancorp, the Lafayette LA peer that overlaps BFST's Acadiana footprint, missed Q3 2026 on credit (released 2026-10-19). Six relationships totaling $19.5M moved to nonaccrual, nonperforming assets rose to $53.7M (1.49% of assets) from $39.2M, and EPS was $1.28 against a $1.51 consensus. Credit is the line BFST sold off on in April 2026 (-4.42%). BFST's own NPAs fell to $109.2M (1.23% of assets) in Q2, and management guided to further NPL reductions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-27 (bmo): -4.42%, the quarter with Q1 NPAs at $123.1M. 2026-07-23: +2.26% when NPAs fell to $109.2M on a $21.0M resolution.
findings.why_not_priced: BFST trades 1% under its 52-week high with all-Buy coverage, so the market is not pricing a regional credit read-through. If it were, BFST would have lagged after 10-19. Its 5-day run-up of +1.9% says it did not.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers on the miss: https://finviz.com/news/405186/home-bancorp-misses-as-credit-costs-overwhelm-record-net-interest-income-management-bets-npas-are-near-peak (same event). Proxy only. HBCP's nonaccruals were idiosyncratic CRE/C&I relationships, and BFST's own document trend runs the other way. Net of the rest of the company, this is a tail risk, not a base case.

findings.finding: Deposit costs turned up in the Gulf South and Texas in Q3 after the Fed's 25 bp hike on 2026-09-16, its first since 2023. Hancock Whitney's deposit costs rose 12 bps to 1.55%, and it guided Q4 to a similar or larger rise, above its July signal of about 10 bps for the half. Third Coast (Texas) saw interest-bearing deposit costs go from 3.41% to 3.49% and NIM fall 13 bps. Home Bancorp's rose 5 bps. BFST pays a high 2.88% on interest-bearing deposits and its Q2 margin gain leaned on cheaper deposits (from 2.95%). Its call assumed only 'no further rate cuts', not a hike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BFST's margin commentary has driven its larger moves (+6.88% Oct 2025, +8.84% Jan 2025). No hiking-cycle reaction exists in the 7-print baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: BFST's Q3 consensus implies margin and NII growth (revenue $93.3M against Q2's ~$91.3M), and the stock is near highs. If the market expected a deposit-cost squeeze and a softer Q4 margin outlook, estimates would have been trimmed after HWC on 10-20.
findings.independence: Third Coast Q3 2026 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001781730/000119312526427908/tcbx-ex99_1.htm. Fed hike: https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fomc-rate-decision-fed-hikes-for-the-first-time-in-three-years/. Investar's NIM rise (finding 1) cuts against this. BFST's rate sensitivity was not retrievable from the 10-Q, so a hike may be neutral or positive for it. Sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: The call guidance this print is measured against goes beyond what consensus seems to embed. Management targeted high single-digit annualized loan growth in Q3 and Q4, falling core expenses, and a 1.25% ROA exiting Q4, against 1.05% core ROAA in Q2. On ~$8.9B of assets, 1.25% is roughly $27-28M a quarter, or about $0.80+ diluted EPS before preferred dividends, versus a $0.74 Q3 bar. Whether Monday reaffirms or walks back that trajectory is the guidance line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2's guide (2026-07-23) the stock moved +2.26% and three analysts raised targets (Stephens $34 to $36, Hovde $32.50 to $36, DA Davidson $33 to $35; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/business-first-bancshares-nasdaqbfst-price-target-raised-to-3500-2026-07-27/).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the July target raises and the run to near 52-week highs reflect it. What is not priced is whether Q3 shows the path, given a Q2 where loans held for investment fell 0.37% and deposits fell 3.1%. The sign is genuinely two-sided, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001624322/000162432226000032/exhibit991_earningsrelease.htm): the CEO says Q2 laid 'the foundation we expected for a strong second half', and $100.3M of low-yield acquired Progressive loans were sold. That is the same company source, not independent.

findings.finding: Philip Jordan, b1BANK's Chief Banking Officer and EVP, resigned voluntarily (8-K Item 5.02, event 2026-09-09, filed 2026-09-11). He had been with the bank since 2008 and leads the unified commercial and retail banking teams, treasury management, mortgage and guaranteed lending. No successor was named. The loss falls on the loan-production engine that the high single-digit growth guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior executive-departure print in the baseline. The stock did not visibly react in September and is near 52-week highs.
findings.why_not_priced: Quiet 8-K with no press release and no successor named. The call is the first time management must address coverage of the commercial book and the Houston pipeline without him. If it were priced, it would show as a September drawdown, and there was none.
findings.independence: Role description: DEF 14A 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1624322/000143774926011695/bfbi20260325_def14a.htm. Same company, not independent. The 8-K says the departure was not due to disagreement.

findings.finding: Insiders sold after the Q2 print, all at $31-32 (roughly today's price). Director George Cummings III sold 20,000 shares on 2026-07-30/31, 10,000 on 08-03 and 3,235 on 08-19. Entities tied to director William Hall sold on 08-05. The General Counsel sold 1,000 on 08-05. EDGAR shows a cluster of eight Form 144s and eleven Form 4s from 07-28 to 09-01, with no open-market buys found.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the filings are public and reported by aggregators. It is filed because the sells sit at the current price, and the selling set its own ceiling near $32 while the stock has since ground to its 52-week high.
findings.independence: https://www.insidertrades.com/alerts/nasdaq-bfst-insider-buying-and-selling-2026-08-26/ (aggregator of the same Form 4s, not independent).

findings.finding: Short interest rose 11.2% to 1.24M shares (4.03% of float) at the 2026-09-30 settlement, with 5.7 days to cover on ~204k shares a day. That is a building but not crowded short into a thin-volume print, which gives a small squeeze tail if the release is clean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. Earlier settlements: about 567k shares (2026-04-30, Equibles) and about 1.1M (2026-06-30, CurvedTrading), so the short has roughly doubled since spring.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set, not something to be priced. It is filed as a modest asymmetry because days to cover is high relative to the 15% realised vol.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The tape (1% under the 52-week high, +3.4% over 20 days, all-Buy coverage) prices a clean quarter. My small net negative cuts mildly against that, but it rests on peer proxies, so it moves p_up only one point under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a proxy loses to a company-level number): Home Bancorp's credit miss shrunk from -0.5 to -0.4, because BFST's own documents show NPAs falling and guided lower.
Rule 5 / core table (macro transmission not confirmed by the company): the deposit-cost / Fed-hike finding shrunk from -0.4 to -0.3.
Rule 3 (a caveat must reach the number): the CBO departure went from -0.2 to -0.15, since the 8-K says no disagreement and the price did not react.

Rule 7 (check positioning before a negative): short interest is 4% of float with 5.7 days to cover and building, so the negatives were shrunk slightly. Insider selling went from -0.2 to -0.1 because it is public, aggregated positioning.
Pessimism-artefact lesson: p_up moved from 48 to 49, because the net negative is built only from proxies and public facts.
Rule 8 / core (understatement is systematic): abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.0, above the 3.85% median historical reaction, since a guidance trajectory (the 1.25% ROA exit) is at stake.
Rule 6 (bar): the bar is two agreeing sources at $0.74, so no cap was needed. Origin and Red River prints after the window moved to outside_window.
